claim: The FTC stated that "[a]n estimated 30 million workers—nearly one in five Americans—are subject to a noncompete."
evidence: An estimated 30 million workers—nearly one in five Americans—are subject to a noncompete.
excerpt:
Noncompetes are a widespread and often exploitative practice imposing contractual conditions that prevent workers from taking a new job or starting a new business. Noncompetes often force workers to either stay in a job they want to leave or bear other significant harms and costs, such as being forced to switch to a lower-paying field, being forced to relocate, being forced to leave the workforce altogether, or being forced to defend against expensive litigation. An estimated 30 million workers—nearly one in five Americans—are subject to a noncompete.
